pride_data.title: Conformational control and DNA binding mechanism of the metazoan origin recognition complex
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study the architecture and conformational state(s) of the Drosophila melanogaster origin replication complex (ORC). Two versions of the ORC were subjected to cross-linking with the amine-reactive reagents, disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS). One was a complex with truncated subunits (“core complex”), one with full-length sequences of all six subunits (“full-length complex”).
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Chemical cross-linking was performed following previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014). Samples were digested using endoproteinase Lys-C and trypsin, digests were fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography and SEC fractions were analyzed by data-dependent LC-MS/MS spectrometry on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos system.  Additional details are provided in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.4, against the sequences of the six target proteins.  Additional search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = -5 to 3 ppm (core complex) or -8 to -1 ppm (full-length complex), MS/MS mass tolerance = 0.2 Da for “common”-type fragment ions and 0.3 Da for “xlink”-type fragment ions. The original scoring scheme of xQuest (Rinner et al., Nat. Methods, 2008) was used.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; structural proteomics; origin recognition complex
